open_obligations: Note that Goel et al.'s risk claim extrapolates a correlational trend.
Check whether constitutional AI feedback models share blind spots with the policies they train.
Check that MCQ-based similarity transfers to free-text harmlessness judgements.
in.other_title: Correlated failures risk: deferring to AI oversight as model blind spots converge
in.rationale: Bai et al. state that reducing human feedback makes it easier to deploy models not tested by humans, with unforeseen failure modes. Goel et al. report more capable LMs make more similar mistakes and argue that as humans defer more to AI oversight, correlated failures pose safety risks; the argument extrapolates a capability-similarity trend measured on MCQ benchmarks.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether replacing human feedback with AI oversight introduces new failure risks, for LLM judges and training on LM annotations

text: The authors state that by reducing the need for human feedback, constitutional methods make it easier to train and deploy AI systems that have not been thoroughly tested and observed by humans, which could lead developers to deploy models with unforeseen failure modes.
title: Less human feedback makes it easier to deploy models not tested or observed by humans
